rules.problem: Omits Hb < 12 (woman) / < 13 (man) from the red box; no sex-specific Hb condition. Clouded consciousness and bleeding synonyms are padding.

rules.rule: Urgent: jaundice with danger signs (changes in skin colour)
rules.problem: Hb < 12 (woman) / < 13 (man) danger sign missing; so a jaundiced anaemic patient is not triaged urgent. Also nothing encodes the 2-day review rule (ALT>=200, INR>=1.5, plts<150, Hb) or hepatitis A / HBsAg referral logic.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable albinism (changes in skin colour)
rules.problem: Requires white hair AND iris hypopigmentation AND generalized congenital achromia; page only says present from birth, involves skin, hair and eyes. Rule will rarely fire.

summary: Most consequential: the urgent-referral rule and its check task omit the red-box criterion Hb < 12 (woman) / < 13 (man). The page's 2-day review/lab-based referral rule and hepatitis A branch are not encoded. Albinism requires hair and eye findings as hard ANDs, and the diagnosis concepts are otherwise faithful.
